cues.zh: 伦敦地铁线路图是伦敦的标志之一，
cues.en: The Tube Map is an icon of London,

cues.zh: 就像大本钟、伦敦塔、伦敦眼和 M&M’s World 一样。
cues.en: just like Big Ben the Tower of London the London Eye and M&Ms World.

cues.zh: 伦敦人和游客都能一眼认出它，
cues.en: It's instantly recognisable to locals and tourists alike

cues.zh: 它为全世界的人熟知、喜爱，也常被拿来恶搞。
cues.en: known and loved and parodied all over the world.

cues.zh: 每隔几个月就会推出一个新版，
cues.en: With a new version coming out every few months,

cues.zh: 有些人简直迷上了地铁线路图，
cues.en: some people are properly obsessed with the Tube Map

cues.zh: 收藏了大量版本，还能看出最细微的差别，
cues.en: with vast collections and can spot the subtlest of differences

cues.zh: 辨别不同版本之间的不同。
cues.en: between different versions.

cues.zh: 呃，看看他们。
cues.en: Eurgh. Look at them.

cues.zh: 一群超级书呆子。
cues.en: Massive bunch of nerds.

cues.zh: 不过，别把这张图的样子当成理所当然。它差点就变成了另一副模样，
cues.en: But don't take this map for granted. This map very nearly looked very different

cues.zh: 而它所描绘的伦敦，也可能因此变得截然不同。
cues.en: and the London it's a map of might have looked very different as a result.

cues.zh: 那么，这张图背后有什么故事呢？
cues.en: So, what is the story behind this map?

cues.zh: 19 世纪中叶，私人运营的地下铁路线
cues.en: In the mid-mid 19th century when privately run underground railway lines

cues.zh: 刚开始在伦敦各处陆续开通时，
cues.en: first started popping down all under London

cues.zh: 人们能找到的地图只有那些
cues.en: the only maps of them available were the ones

cues.zh: 由各家私营公司自己出版的地图，
cues.en: published by the private companies themselves

cues.zh: 上面自家线路标得清晰醒目；至于竞争对手的线路，要是他们愿意标出来，
cues.en: showing their own services in clear bold, and rival services, if they felt like it

cues.zh: 就用细淡的线条画，免得你注意到。
cues.en: in narrow faint lines they didn't want you to notice.

cues.zh: 因为竞争公司常常争夺同一批乘客
cues.en: Because rival companies were often competing for the same passengers

cues.zh: 所以他们经常故意不配合。
cues.en: they very often went out of their way to be uncooperative.

cues.zh: 这条环线由两家互相仇视的竞争公司运营。
cues.en: This circular route was operated by two rival companies who hated each other.

cues.zh: 大都会铁路顺时针方向运行列车
cues.en: The Metropolitan Railway ran trains clockwise

cues.zh: 而名字相似得令人困惑的大都会区域铁路
cues.en: and the confusingly similarly named Metropolitan District Railway

cues.zh: 则逆时针方向运行列车。说来话长。
cues.en: ran trains anti-clockwise. Long story.

cues.zh: 如果你想只坐一站，却从错误的售票处买了票
cues.en: If you wanted to go just one stop but you bought your ticket from the wrong booth

cues.zh: 你就得绕环线走一大圈。
cues.en: you had to go the long way round the circle.

cues.zh: 这类不配合的例子还有很多。
cues.en: And there were plenty more examples of uncooperativeness where this came from.

cues.zh: 比如，如果你想在Bank站换乘
cues.en: For example, if you wanted to change trains at Bank station

cues.zh: 就得坐电梯上到街面，过马路，再买一张票
cues.en: you had to take the lift up to the street, cross the road, buy another ticket

cues.zh: 然后再坐电梯一路下去。
cues.en: and then take the lift all the way back down again.

cues.zh: 伦敦的地下铁道原本可以发挥更大的作用，
cues.en: London's underground Railways could have been so much more

cues.zh: 吸引更多的乘客，
cues.en: useful and attracted so many more passengers

cues.zh: 前提是它们能作为一个协调的系统整体运营。
cues.en: if they were all run together as a coordinated system.

cues.zh: 但这需要一个财力极其雄厚的人才能实现。
cues.en: But it would take someone with a colossal bank account to make that happen.

cues.zh: 对伦敦人来说幸运的是，1902年这个人出现了，
cues.en: Fortunately for Londoners, in 1902 that someone came along

cues.zh: 他就是雄心勃勃的美国铁路大亨 Charles Tyson Yerkes，
cues.en: in the form of ambitious American railway Tycoon Charles Tyson Yerkes

cues.zh: 他不仅账户资金极其雄厚，留着极其浓密的大胡子，
cues.en: who had a colossal bank account, a colossal moustache

cues.zh: 还有一个叫 Guttridge 的妻子。
cues.en: and a wife called Guttridge.

cues.zh: 这是我妻子。来，告诉大家你的名字。
cues.en: This is my wife. Go on, tell them your name.

cues.zh: Guttridge。
cues.en: Guttridge.

cues.zh: Charles 的想法非常具有美国风格，那就是运营一个铁路网络，
cues.en: Charles's very American idea was to run a railway network

cues.zh: 一组纵横穿梭于整座城市的线路，
cues.en: a group of lines stretching in all directions across the city

cues.zh: 你只需买一张票，就能从一条线路出发，在另一条线路上结束行程。
cues.en: where with one ticket, you could start your journey on one line and end it on another.

cues.zh: 于是他成立了一家名为 Underground Electric Railways of London 的公司，
cues.en: So he set up a company called Underground Electric Railways of London

cues.zh: 简称 UERL。
cues.en: Or UERL for short.

cues.zh: 或者简写成 ooerrl。
cues.en: Or ooerrl for shorter.

cues.zh: 他带着囤积的全部财富，开始了一场地下铁路的疯狂收购
cues.en: With all the money he'd piled, up he went on an underground railway shopping spree

cues.zh: 其中还包括四条尚未完工的线路。
cues.en: including four lines that hadn't even been finished yet.

cues.zh: 到1905年11月，Charles Yerkes已自豪地拥有查令十字、
cues.en: By November 1905, Charles Yerkes was the proud owner of the Charing Cross,

cues.zh: 尤斯顿与汉普斯特德、大都会区域、
cues.en: Euston and Hampstead, Metropolitan District,

cues.zh: 大北方、布朗普顿与皮卡迪利、贝克街与滑铁卢等铁路。
cues.en: Great Northern, Brompton and Piccadilly, Baker Street and Waterloo Railways.

cues.zh: 而到了1905年12月，他就去世了。
cues.en: And by December 1905, he was dead.

cues.zh: 他这一死真是高明，
cues.en: With the very shrewd move of dying,

cues.zh: 省得偿还自己欠下的巨额债务。
cues.en: he avoided having to pay back any of the huge debts he'd built up.

cues.zh: 但他在伦敦打造地下铁路网的梦想已然成真。
cues.en: But his dream of creating an underground network in London had come true.

cues.zh: UERL是一个真正整合的系统，有统一票务
cues.en: The UERL was a properly integrated system with common ticketing

cues.zh: 和外观极为相似的车站建筑。
cues.en: and station buildings that looked really similar.

cues.zh: 而像样的铁路网需要一张像样的地图。
cues.en: And a proper network needed a proper map.

cues.zh: 于是在 1908 年，UERL 发布了这张图。
cues.en: And so in 1908 the UERL published this.

cues.zh: 这是第一张涵盖伦敦所有地下铁路线的地图，
cues.en: The first map that showed all the underground lines in London

cues.zh: 全部画在了一张图上，甚至包括不属于 UERL 的线路。
cues.en: mapped on one map, including the ones UERL didn't own.

cues.zh: 它带来了一些非常实用的创新。
cues.en: It had some really handy innovations.

cues.zh: 每条线路的粗细都相同，且各用不同的颜色区分。
cues.en: Each line was given equal thickness, and each line was given a different colour.

cues.zh: 这些特征我们如今都已习以为常，
cues.en: Features that are familiar to us today

cues.zh: 尽管当时的配色大家可能不太熟悉。
cues.en: Even if the colours aren't too familiar.

cues.zh: Piccadilly 线居然是黄色的！？哈哈哈哈！！
cues.en: The Piccadilly line in yellow!? Hahahahaha!!

cues.zh: 这张包含整个线网的完整地图非常实用，
cues.en: This complete map of the whole network was very useful

cues.zh: 但读起来却并不轻松。
cues.en: But it wasn't very easy to read.

cues.zh: 上面画满了所有的地铁线、道路、地标，
cues.en: With all the Tube lines and roads and landmarks

cues.zh: 还有……陆海军联营百货商场？
cues.en: and... army and navy and auxiliary stores?

cues.zh: 信息塞得太满，显得杂乱无章，
cues.en: It was a messy clutter with too much information

cues.zh: 看起来就像一盘乱糟糟的意大利面。
cues.en: and looked like a plate of spaghetti.

cues.zh: 问题在于，要想绘制一张涵盖整个线网、
cues.en: The problem was, the task of creating a map of the whole network

cues.zh: 既实用又清晰易读的地图，向来是一件公认的苦差事。
cues.en: that was both useful and easy to read was a notoriously difficult one.

cues.zh: 当时，许多公司都发布了自己的伦敦网络地图
cues.en: Lots of companies at this time published their own maps of London's network

cues.zh: 各有各的做法，有些还相当离谱。
cues.en: each with their own approaches, some of them bonkers.

cues.zh: 我最喜欢的是这张：Max Gill 的《奇妙地下地图》。
cues.en: This one's my favorite: The Wonderground Map by Max Gill.

cues.zh: 既精细得惊人，又完全没用得惊人。
cues.en: Simultaneously incredibly detailed and incredibly completely useless.

cues.zh: 而要把整个系统画进一张图，只会变得更更难。
cues.en: Mapping the entire system was only about to get even difficulter.

cues.zh: 到20年代初，伦敦地铁已经开始
cues.en: By the early 20s the London Underground had begun

cues.zh: 不受控制地向四面八方蔓延，伸进远郊。
cues.en: sprawling uncontrollably out in all directions into the distant suburbs.

cues.zh: 为了管理这种扩张，UERL 任命了新的宣传主管 Frank Pick。
cues.en: To help manage this growth, the UERL appointed a new head of publicity, Frank Pick.

cues.zh: Pick 痴迷于地铁的企业形象
cues.en: Pick was obsessed with the Tube's corporate identity

cues.zh: 就是让整个系统感觉更……统一。
cues.en: the notion that the whole system should feel more... togethery.

cues.zh: 正是 Pick 的主意，让每个车站都有了圆标
cues.en: It was Pick's idea for every station to have a roundel,

cues.zh: 那个红圈配蓝线的标志性 logo。
cues.en: the iconic logo with the red circle and blue line.

cues.zh: 而每一个标志都要用同一种字体
cues.en: And for every sign to use the same font with the

cues.zh: 字母O要圆得完美，字母I上方的小点要像小菱形。
cues.en: perfectly round O's and the little diamonds for dots above the I's.

cues.zh: 还要委托制作那些漂亮的海报
cues.en: And to commission all those lovely posters

cues.zh: 就是你中产朋友们厨房里挂的那种。
cues.en: that your middle class friends have in their kitchens.

cues.zh: 最重要的是，Pick希望每一份传单、每一张海报，在每一列火车上
cues.en: Most importantly Pick wanted every leaflet and every poster on every train

cues.zh: 在每一个站台、每一个车站，都用同一套地图设计。
cues.en: on every platform and every station to use the same map design.

cues.zh: 于是，为了寻找完美地图，
cues.en: And so, in search of the perfect map,

cues.zh: Pick找到了一位设计师，名字叫……大家一起喊……
cues.en: Pick turned to a designer named... altogether now...

cues.zh: -（观众）Harry Beck。- Frank Stingemore。啊！
cues.en: - (audience) Harry Beck. - Frank Stingemore. Aaah!

cues.zh: Frank Stingemore 1924年的地图
cues.en: Frank Stingemore's map from 1924

cues.zh: 只把泰晤士河当作地理参照，别的什么都没有。
cues.en: used the River Thames as a geographical reference and nothing else.

cues.zh: 没有道路，没有地标，什么都没有。只有一片素净的米色背景。
cues.en: No roads, no landmarks, no nothing. Just a plain beige background.

cues.zh: 易读性是 Stingemore 的首要考量，
cues.en: With easiness of reading at the top of Stingemore's priority list

cues.zh: 所以他的地图做了件基本算作弊的事。
cues.en: his map did something that was basically cheating.

cues.zh: 为了塞下所有细节，Stingemore走了个偷懒的捷径
cues.en: To fit all the detail in Stingemore took the naughty shortcut

cues.zh: 干脆不按比例画远处的郊区。
cues.en: of not bothering to draw the distant suburbs to scale.

cues.zh: 比如，这些站——就在我们现在叫北线的那条线上——
cues.en: For example, these stations on what we now call the Northern line

cues.zh: 被不诚实地挤在一起，排成一条完全虚构的直线。
cues.en: were bunched dishonestly together in a totally fictional straight line.

cues.zh: 但问题是……关键是……
cues.en: But the thing is though.. that's the thing...

cues.zh: 关键是，这个，这才是关键……
cues.en: The thing is, this, this is the thing...

cues.zh: 关键是……这根本不重要！
cues.en: The thing is... this didn't matter!

cues.zh: 对于想从A站到B站的乘客来说
cues.en: For passengers trying to get from station A to station B

cues.zh: 这张图依然完美地完成了它的使命。
cues.en: this map still served its purpose perfectly well.

cues.zh: 除非你是开火车的，否则你干嘛要知道
cues.en: Unless you were driving the train, why did you need to know the exact length

cues.zh: 每一段轨道的精确长度或精确弯曲度？
cues.en: or exact bendiness of each bit of track?

cues.zh: 说起来，就算你是开火车的
cues.en: Come to think of it, even if you're driving the train

cues.zh: 你也并不真的需要知道这些，对吧？
cues.en: you don't really need to know that either do you?

cues.zh: Frank Pick对Stingemore的地图非常满意
cues.en: Frank Pick was very happy with Stingemore's map

cues.zh: 公众也很满意。
cues.en: and the public were happy with it too.

cues.zh: Stingemore 的创新表明，一张地图即便比例失真，
cues.en: Stingemore's innovation had shown that a map could still be useful

cues.zh: 也依然可以非常实用。
cues.en: even if the scale was distorted.

cues.zh: 正是这个理念启发了另一位设计师，
cues.en: And it was this concept that inspired another designer

cues.zh: 做出了更加激进的大胆尝试。他的名字是……
cues.en: to do something even more radical And his name was...

cues.zh: -（是 Harry Beck 吗？）-（肯定是。）
cues.en: - (Is it Harry Beck?) - (It's got to be.)

cues.zh: -（上次就不是。）-（我觉得就是 Harry Beck。）
cues.en: - (It wasn't last time.) - (I think it's Harry Beck.)

cues.zh: -（我们要猜 Harry Beck 吗？）-（万一不是他呢？）
cues.en: - (Shall we say Harry Beck?) - (What if it's not Harry Beck?)

cues.zh: -（我觉得这次肯定是他。）-（那就猜 Harry Be……）
cues.en: - (I think it is this time.) - (Let's say Harry Be...)

cues.zh: Harry Beck！
cues.en: Harry Beck!

cues.zh: Henry Charles Beck，那些并不存在的朋友叫他 Harry，
cues.en: Henry Charles Beck, known as Harry to his no friends

cues.zh: 当时是 UERL 一名 29 岁的工程制图员。
cues.en: was a 29 year old technical draftsman working at UERL.

cues.zh: 他的工作是绘制地铁信号系统的图纸。
cues.en: It was his job to draw up diagrams of the Tube's signaling systems.

cues.zh: 然而到了 1931 年他被裁员了，这份工作也就告一段落。
cues.en: And then it wasn't his job anymore when he got made redundant in 1931.

cues.zh: Harry 一定非常怀念原来的工作，因为离开 UERL 之后，
cues.en: Harry must have really missed his old job, because after leaving the UERL

cues.zh: 他在业余时间捣鼓起了一个极其极客的、和老本行相关的项目。
cues.en: he spent his spare time working on an extremely nerdy work-related project.

cues.zh: 他带着极客范儿脑补了一下
cues.en: He nerdly imagined what it would look like

cues.zh: 如果把伦敦地铁的所有车站
cues.en: if all the stations on the London Underground were represented

cues.zh: 画成电路图那样连起来会是什么样。
cues.en: connected like in a circuit diagram.

cues.zh: 他见过完全脱离地理信息的单条线路条形图。
cues.en: He'd seen strip maps of individual lines that totally ignored geography.

cues.zh: 把它们全整合在一起能有多难呢？
cues.en: How hard could it be to combine them all together?

cues.zh: 如果说 Stingemore 的做法只是对比例尺略微动了点手脚
cues.en: While Stingemore's approach was to be a little bit naughty with scale

cues.zh: 那 Beck 的态度就是：比例尺算个【哔——】。
cues.en: Beck's approach was that scale could absolutely go [BEEP] itself.

cues.zh: Harry 在画整个网络时只用了笔直的线条
cues.en: Harry drew the entire network using only strrrraight lines

cues.zh: 要么垂直，要么水平，要么呈 45 度角。
cues.en: that were vertical, horizontal or at 45 degrees.

cues.zh: 这是他的一张草稿
cues.en: Here's one of his rough drafts

cues.zh: 他在上面擦掉旧线条，换成了更平直的线。
cues.en: where he rubbed out lines and replaced them with straighter ones.

cues.zh: 当他终于完成时，效果是这样的。
cues.en: When he finally finished it looked like this.

cues.zh: 一个优雅而色彩丰富的方案
cues.en: An elegant colourful design

cues.zh: 伦敦市中心的车站分布均匀
cues.en: with the stations in central London spaced evenly apart

cues.zh: 而郊区的车站则紧凑地挤在一起。
cues.en: and the suburban stations bunched up close together.

cues.zh: 没有放过任何机会，确保对称、等距和并行。
cues.en: No opportunity was missed for symmetry equal spacing and parallelity.

cues.zh: 如果把他的设计比作比例地图，
cues.en: If you compare his design to a scale map

cues.zh: 你就能看出它有多不按比例，坦率地说，有多疯狂。
cues.en: you can see just how not to scale and frankly mad it was.

cues.zh: Harry所谓的“行程规划图”并非地图——而是一张示意图。
cues.en: Harry's so-called "Journey Planner" was not a map - it was a diagram.

cues.zh: 但就它想要完成的非常具体的任务而言，示意图胜过地图。
cues.en: But for the very specific job it was trying to do, a diagram was better than a map.

cues.zh: 通过完全忽略比例的概念，
cues.en: By totally ignoring the concept of scale,

cues.zh: 他不仅能够容纳所有车站，
cues.en: he was able not only to fit all the stations in

cues.zh: 而且使它比Stingemore的地图更容易阅读。
cues.en: but to make it much easier to read than Stingemore's map.

cues.zh: 它还给人一种印象，
cues.en: It also gave the impression

cues.zh: 一个 cohesive、全面、协调、互联的系统。
cues.en: of a cohesive, comprehensive, coordinated, connected system.

cues.zh: 它看起来也很棒。
cues.en: It also looked awesome.

cues.zh: Harry对自己非常满意，然后他想到了一件事……
cues.en: Harry was very pleased with himself and a thought occurred to him...

cues.zh: 这应该成为伦敦交通的官方地图。
cues.en: This should be the official map for London Transport.

cues.zh: Frank Pick会喜欢这个的！
cues.en: Frank Pick is going to love this!

cues.zh: 于是在1931年晚些时候，Harry大步走回UERL的办公室
cues.en: And so, later in 1931, Harry marched back into the offices of the UERL

cues.zh: 这家公司现在叫伦敦交通局
cues.en: which was now called London Transport

cues.zh: 向Frank Pick展示他的线路图。
cues.en: to show his diagram to Frank Pick.

cues.zh: 但Harry错了。
cues.en: But Harry was wrong.

cues.zh: Frank Pick一点也不喜欢Harry的地图。
cues.en: Frank Pick didn't love Harry's map at all.

cues.zh: Pick拒绝出版Beck的地图，理由是它“不准确”
cues.en: Pick refused to publish Beck's map on the grounds that it was "inaccurate"

cues.zh: 而且公众看不懂。
cues.en: and that the public wouldn't understand it.

cues.zh: 无比例尺的做法确实有个缺点。
cues.en: There was indeed a disadvantage to the scale-free approach.
